Goal: use skills to stop the most common kinds of AI slop: guessed fixes, tests that prove nothing, and "done" with no evidence. First you discover skills with your client's built-in skill tools. Then you load three popular public skills and apply them to a real bug.

Part Time You invoke
A. Discover skills with built-in tools 10 min /skills (VS Code and app), /af and /skills reload (app)
B. Load the public skills 5 min npm run setup -- superpowers, npm run skills
C. Practice: debug, test first, verify 25-35 min /systematic-debugging, /test-driven-development, /verification-before-completion

Set up first: follow the environment guide. Watch the four Lab 2 GIFs on the workshop site.

The three public skills

From obra/superpowers, one of the most installed skill collections on skills.sh. They are public skills, not Copilot built-ins.

Skill Slop it prevents What you should see
/systematic-debugging A fix that is a guess Reproduction, file:line evidence, one testable cause, no edits yet
/test-driven-development Tests that pass on broken code A meaningful assertion failure before the repair, a pass after
/verification-before-completion "All done!" with no proof Fresh command output, real exit codes, a reviewed diff

Popular is not the same as correct. Read the skill files and check the results.

Part A: discover skills with built-in tools

A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file. Clients find skills in these places:

Scope Locations
This project .github/skills/, .claude/skills/, .agents/skills/
You, in every project ~/.copilot/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/, ~/.agents/skills/

Your client may also ship built-in skills. Use its own tools to see what is actually loaded. Do not rely on memory or a list from someone else.

VS Code

  1. Open any workspace, start a Local chat and type /skills. This opens the Configure Skills menu. Note the built-in, personal and workspace entries.
  2. Type / on its own to see which skills appear in the slash picker.

GitHub Copilot app

  1. In an Interactive session, type /skills to list and manage skills.

  2. Use the built-in Agent Finder skill to search for anti-slop skills. Ask it to compare candidates. Do not install anything yet.

    /af Find popular public agent skills that stop guessed fixes, tests that prove nothing and unverified completion claims. Show source repository, license and install method for each. Do not install anything.

  3. After you add skill files during a session, run /skills reload.

Checkpoint: you can name every skill your client has loaded and say where each one came from. A duplicate name in a personal folder is a warning sign.

Part B: load the public skills

Option 1: bundled, pinned copies (use this for the lab)

From the lab directory:

npm.cmd run setup -- superpowers
npm.cmd run skills
code -n .\work\superpowers

Setup copies the three complete upstream skill folders, their MIT license and a manifest into work\superpowers\.github\skills. npm run skills checks all 15 files against SHA-256 hashes pinned to upstream commit 2ce8aa15d05bd57213e6f746f953aafb7ded7a8b. No network, hooks or global install is needed.

Then confirm loading in your client:

  • VS Code: open work\superpowers itself, start a fresh Local chat, and type /skills. All three must point to this workspace's .github/skills.
  • Copilot app: add work\superpowers as a local repository, start an Interactive session, and run /skills reload then /skills.

Finally, ask the agent to name the skill path it would use:

Which loaded skill applies to the quantity bug in BRIEF.md? Name the exact SKILL.md path you would load. Do not edit files.

Check tool activity for .github/skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md in this workspace. A similar-sounding answer does not prove the skill loaded.

Option 2: add them to your own project

  • Skills-only ZIP: download anti-slop-public-skills.zip from the workshop site. Copy the three whole folders (not just SKILL.md) into your project's .github/skills/. Keep LICENSE and manifest.json with them.

  • Skills CLI: fetches the latest upstream version, not the pinned copy, so review what it installs.

    npx skills add https://github.com/obra/superpowers --skill systematic-debugging -a github-copilot
npx skills add https://github.com/obra/superpowers --skill test-driven-development -a github-copilot
npx skills add https://github.com/obra/superpowers --skill verification-before-completion -a github-copilot

    It installs into .agents/skills/ in the project, or into ~/.copilot/skills/ with -g. Confirm the result with /skills.

Never overwrite an existing skill with the same name. Do not install these again inside work\superpowers, which already has them, because duplicate names make it unclear which copy ran.

Part C: practice: debug, test first, verify

Scenario: the same cart bug as Lab 1 Part A (quantity is ignored), in a fresh workspace. Compare how skills shape the work.

From the work\superpowers terminal:

npm.cmd run check -- --baseline

Expect 3/7 pass, 4 intended failures, BASELINE CONFIRMED, not solved.

1. Debug: investigate before editing

/systematic-debugging Read BRIEF.md and src/cart.mjs. Reproduce the quantity defect, cite file:line evidence, and state one testable cause. Do not edit yet. Keep investigation inside this disposable workspace.

Check it: priceCents: 250, qty: 3 should give 750, but the starter returns 250. Confirm the cited line yourself. Then approve changes to src/cart.mjs and src/cart.test.mjs only.

2. Test first: red before green

/test-driven-development Follow BRIEF.md. Add at least four node:test cases to src/cart.test.mjs. Preserve existing behavior and cover quantity, invalid input and overflow. Run npm test with cart.mjs unchanged; stop for review of the red output. Do not delete existing starter or learner work.

Reject tests that are all green on the broken starter, syntax or import errors posing as "red", and assertions that copy the buggy behavior. After you see a meaningful failure:

I approve the minimal cart repair under BRIEF.md. Change only src/cart.mjs; keep the test assertions and legacy pricing unchanged. Run the complete learner test suite after the repair.

3. Verify: fresh evidence, honest limits

/verification-before-completion Run npm test and npm run check now. Report actual exit codes, passed/failed counts and unresolved issues. Inspect git diff and git status --short, including untracked tests. Do not commit or change acceptance tooling.

Then run them yourself:

npm.cmd test
npm.cmd run check
git --no-pager diff
git --no-pager status --short

You need VERIFIED: 7/7, exit 0. The checker also replays your tests against the original code: a suite that passes on both fails. The skill files must stay unchanged.

Evidence to keep

  • The skills your client listed, and where each came from (Part A)
  • The exact loaded SKILL.md path in this workspace (Part B)
  • Root cause with file:line before any edit
  • A red test run before the repair
  • Fresh VERIFIED: 7/7, exit 0, and a reviewed diff
  • Anything still unverified, stated plainly

Safety notes

  • Skills are guidance, not a security boundary. Keep tool approvals on.
  • Upstream text sometimes says superpowers:<name>. That is plugin notation; here, use the plain name the picker shows.
  • Do not run upstream example scripts, delete existing work, or change unrelated code to satisfy a skill.
  • A GIF is not proof that a skill ran. Tool activity and your own test runs are.
